title: A Pre-registered TESS Sector 110 Test of Two Transit-like Signals in TIC 4206066
description:
This record pre-registers a test of two transit-like signals in TESS data of the nearby K dwarf TIC 4206066. Signal A repeats every 3.18 days. Signal B repeats every 11.13 days; it is more tentative and has less archival support. Both signals were selected after the archival data had been inspected, so those data are not an independent test.

TESS observes the star again in Sector 110, from 2026-10-31 to 2026-11-26, at 2-minute cadence. These data did not exist when the protocol was written, so they give an independent test. The protocol fixes in advance the predicted transit times (nine for A, three for B, with an uncertainty of about 4 minutes, 1σ), the expected depths and the processing of the light curve. A fixed rule gives each signal one of four outcomes: recovered, inconsistent, excluded, or insufficient data. The protocol also fixes a timing check and a pixel-level check of whether the position of signal A is compatible with TIC 4206066. Frozen code computes the outcomes; the protocol text decides which runs and inputs are valid.

Start with PREREG_S110_SHORT.pdf, a three-page summary with one figure. The full protocol, PREREG_S110_FINAL.pdf, gives the exact rules and takes precedence. The ZIP file contains the frozen code, the software environment, the calibrations, the archival test runs, checksums and the LaTeX source. Recovering a signal in Sector 110 would not prove that it is a planet, and an undecided result would not show that it is not.

title: Two Transit-like Signals in TESS Photometry of the Nearby K Dwarf TIC 4206066
description: Preprint of a Research Note prepared for submission to the Research Notes of the AAS. Abstract: I report two transit-like signals in TESS photometry of the late-K dwarf TIC 4206066 (StKM 1-561), found in Sector 98 and traced back to Sectors 6 and 32. The 3.18 d signal (23 transits, ~500 ppm) corresponds to a 1.4 +/- 0.1 Earth-radius planet if it orbits the target. Vetting, localization, and Gaia astrometry, photometry, and radial velocities leave a planet transiting an unresolved bound companion as the main alternative host scenario; TRICERATOPS gives FPP = 0.03-0.04, mostly from companions these data disfavor. The lower-significance 11.13 d signal (~2.2 Earth radii if on the target; ~3 sigma in a post hoc test) is reported with a tentative ephemeris. No statistical validation is claimed. Supporting data and code: doi:10.5281/zenodo.22967099.

title: Supporting data and code for "Two Transit-like Signals in TESS Photometry of the Nearby K Dwarf TIC 4206066"
description: Supporting research materials for the manuscript "Two Transit-like Signals in TESS Photometry of the Nearby K Dwarf TIC 4206066" by Pavel Rabtsevich. The study examines TESS photometry from Sectors 6, 32, and 98 and reports a 3.18-day planet candidate and a tentative 11.13-day transit-like signal. The host of the 3.18-day signal remains uncertain, with an unresolved bound companion remaining an alternative. No statistical validation is claimed. The upload consists of README.md and three ZIP archives containing the supporting materials (input product list, per-transit measurements, the archival recovery test, the TRICERATOPS false-positive runs and their decomposition by companion mass, companion limits, pixel localisation, the 11.13-day analysis, the data behind Figure 1, and software environments). Data and documentation: CC BY 4.0; original code: MIT; third-party materials keep their original terms (see README.md).
